notes.summary: The page continues a discussion with Chow's lemma and the Main existence theorem from a Picard-schemes talk, then states Corollary 2 about existence, separatedness and finite-type connected components of Pic under its stated Problem A condition. Its N.B. discusses the words quasi-affine and affine, asks for a couterexample in two specified settings, and connects the latter question with effectivity for a finite morphism. The marginal note says impossible if X smooth! The final block defines Problem A through representability of a flatness functor and refers to the proof of existence of Hilbert schemes. These are summaries of the page; no proof verification is claimed.
author_checks: The proof does not give any evidence towards the fact that in the theorem, one could replace ``quasi-affine'' by ``affine'' .
It would be interesting to have a couterexample
